headline: Cortez, Alabama survive Leavitt's rally, 21-20
dek: Alabama evens its record at 1-1 while Boston College falls to 0-2 in the Eastern Atlantic race.
body: With 35 seconds left and Boston College at the Alabama 35, Darius Rivas lined up a 52-yard field goal to steal it, but the kick sailed wide right and Alabama took over at its 42 with five seconds remaining to seal a 21-20 win.

The first quarter produced only punts and a pair of missed field goals, then Alabama struck twice in the second quarter: James Cortez hit Adrian Curry on a five-yard touchdown pass at 9:42, and after Sam Leavitt answered with a seven-yard strike to Sedmaj Flemming, Cortez found Ethan Monroe on a one-yard jet sweep at 1:52 for a 14-7 halftime lead. Boston College trimmed it to 14-10 on a 33-yard Rivas field goal early in the third, but Cortez capped an 8-play, 74-yard drive with a 21-yard Keith Adams Jr. touchdown run at 5:01 to push the margin to 11. Leavitt drove the Eagles 80 yards in 13 plays for a one-yard touchdown pass to Will Graves III at 8:34 of the fourth, then a short field set up a 26-yard Rivas field goal at 4:20 to make it a one-point game.

Alabama won despite being outgained 405-345 and holding the ball barely 27 minutes, because Cortez was efficient at 19-of-30 for 252 yards and a touchdown while Leavitt needed 47 throws for 292 yards and two scores. The Tide converted just 3 of 10 third downs but went 1-for-1 on fourth down and committed zero penalties, while Boston College was 7-of-15 on third down and 2-for-2 on fourth down but left nine points on the board with three missed field goals. Adams Jr. added 40 rushing yards and the go-ahead touchdown, and Earle Hampton caught five passes for 76 yards, while Leavitt's top target Jayden Skeete finished with four catches for 62 yards and a 34-yard explosive play late in the first half.

The victory lifts Alabama to 1-1 and keeps it third in the Eastern Atlantic behind division leader Texas, while Boston College drops to 0-2 and last in the division with its power-poll ranking sliding from 10 to 14. Alabama's defense, still last in the league at 502 yards allowed per game, bent but forced the final miss, and the staff will prepare for a home date against 0-2 Michigan State next week. Boston College must regroup on the road at 1-1 Colorado, where Bo MacCormick's 107 rushing yards on the season will be needed to jumpstart an offense that ranks 16th in total yards.
turningPoint: Rivas' 52-yard field goal attempt with nine seconds left in the fourth quarter sailed wide right, preserving Alabama's 21-20 lead.
byTheNumbers: Alabama converted 1 of 1 fourth downs while Boston College went 2 of 2, but the Tide's lone conversion came on the game's final drive to ice the clock.
Boston College missed three field goals (47, 45, 52 yards) totaling nine points, the exact margin of Alabama's largest lead.
Cortez averaged 8.4 yards per attempt with zero interceptions; Leavitt averaged 6.2 yards per attempt on 17 more throws.
The Eagles held a 32:27 to 27:33 time-of-possession edge and a 21-20 first-down advantage but turned neither into a lead.

unsungHero.name: Jason Nash
unsungHero.why: The safety knocked down Leavitt's third-down pass intended for Reed Harris and tackled Nedrick Bolden on the ensuing first-down play, forcing the fourth-down conversion that set up the final field-goal attempt.
